sentences.text: Goniopholis looked like modern crocodiles and probably hunted by waiting in the water.
Its back featured two lines of large rectangular scutes connected by a peg and groove system, unlike the skin of living relatives.
One species, G. kiplingi, carries the name of author Rudyard Kipling to honor his love of science.
The skull of G. kiplingi measured 475.6 mm, ranking it among the biggest goniopholidids.
Fossil eggs attributed to Goniopholis have been discovered in Late Jurassic rocks in Portugal.
The type species G. crassidens comes from the Berriasian of England, while G. simus from NW Germany might be the same animal.
G. baryglyphaeus from the Kimmeridgian of Portugal represents the oldest known member of the genus.
Scientists found a partial skeleton of an unnamed Goniopholis in the Angeac-Charente bonebed in France.
Bone structure and stable isotope data suggest Goniopholis was ectothermic.
Richard Owen created the genus name Goniopholis in 1841.
This animal lived between the Bathonian and Santonian stages, roughly 168.2 to 83.6 million years ago.
